_about: Resource budget for the Pip product firmware (--features physical-st7789, release, thumbv6m RP2040-Zero). Checked without hardware by `just fw-budget` (scripts/firmware-budget.mjs) and in the firmware CI job. Rebaselined on 2026-11-05 for the RP2040-Zero build (#179) from the ELF the build produced. The stack figures are the static estimate only: the RISC-V version of this check matched a unit within 4 B, but the ARM estimate has NOT been cross-checked on a board yet (pending the hardware test in #179). To change a limit on purpose, edit it here with the reason; see docs/virtual-pip.md (Hardware parity).

app_image_bytes.why: Loadable sections (vector table, boot2, text, rodata, data) were 300,120 B with the RGB LED (290,356 B without it: the LED engine and its timer interrupt are about 3 KB, the rest is the compiler re-deciding what to inline around the new `Message` variant). About 5% headroom; flash is 2 MB, so this is a regression tripwire, not the physical limit.

asset_blob_bytes.why: The compiled asset blob was 127,253 B. The hard cap (ASSET_BLOB_CAP_BYTES, 131,072 B) is read from firmware/pip/src/internals.rs and checked too; this is a tighter early warning.

static_ram_bytes.why: Static RAM (data + bss) was 150,044 B (the interrupt-shared USB device is about 1 KiB of that, the LED driver 44 B), of which the frame buffer is 115,200 B. Everything above it comes out of the stack region, which is the rest of the 264 KB of SRAM.

stack_region_bytes.why: The stack region (_stack_start - _stack_end) was 120,336 B. It must not shrink: the boot peak below leaves about 10 KiB free.

default_frame_bytes.why: Any function with a bigger frame must be listed in large_frames with its own ceiling, so a new large frame is a decision, not an accident.

worst_stack_bytes.why: Direct call chain from main was 109,260 B (the boot parse: load_assets with the inlined AssetBlob::parse and the postcard Vec<SceneDef,8> visitor, which `main` runs before run_mode so its 7.5 KiB frame is not stacked under it). Once the loop runs the chain is about 25 KiB. About 4% headroom for the regression gate. Static estimate, not yet measured on a unit.

indirect_allowance_bytes.why: Calls through a register (trait objects, fn pointers) cannot be followed. Carried over from the RISC-V build (deepest chain 384 B, 2.5x margin), not re-derived for ARM yet.

interrupt_margin_bytes.why: Added on top of the deepest traced interrupt path (interrupt_paths: the rotary GPIO, USBCTRL_IRQ and LED timer handlers, which share a priority and so do not nest) for the parts of an interrupt that are not followed, including the 32 B exception frame the core stacks.

stack_margin_bytes.why: The estimated peak plus the allowances plus this margin must fit the stack region. 8 KiB (down from 16 KiB on the C3, which had 162 KiB of stack): the 264 KB SRAM leaves 10.8 KiB over the boot peak, and at that peak no interrupt is live and no indirect call runs. Raise the margin again once the ARM estimate is checked against a unit.

large_frames.why: Boot only: the inlined AssetBlob::parse holds the manifest (Vec<SceneDef,8> and the bitmap table). It sets the stack peak.
Boot only: postcard builds the Vec<SceneDef,8> by value, below load_assets.
The run loop's locals; lives for the whole session.
Owns the peripherals and the display buffers' setup (including the 4 KiB mipidsi staging buffer); lives for the whole session.
Input handling with the inlined scene transitions.
Frame decode and dispatch with the inlined handlers (3,720 B with the LedSettings arm; it was 3,232 B before).
Boot only: postcard builds the bitmap table.
Postcard encode of the whole `Message` enum (1,112 B). With the LedSettings variant the compiler no longer inlines it into `send_within`, which dropped from 1,664 B to 616 B.

int64_division_allowlist.why: LED refresh (50 Hz): the clock turns the 64-bit microsecond counter into the same milliseconds the run loop uses, so the fade and a press flash stay in step across the 71-minute wrap of a 32-bit microsecond count. About a thousand cycles a tick. Known debt, like IO_IRQ_BANK0.
Rotary interrupt: the clock turns the 64-bit microsecond counter into milliseconds (a software loop on the M0+). Known debt; keep it cheap.
The run loop's clock and window arithmetic (once per tick, not per pixel).
Animation time scaling, once per frame. Known debt.
Gaze interpolation, once per frame. Known debt.
Line setup (slope), per line not per pixel. Known debt.
Per-sprite setup, not per pixel. Known debt; before PR #150 the same class of call in the pixel path made frames 4x slower.
The scene loop length (`frame_count * 1000 * fps.den / fps.num`, compositor.rs), once per frame, not per pixel.
